pr.title: Use VNNI K layout in AMX attention
Use VNNI K layout in AMX attention
pr.head: 0ee8671d35

short_version: PR 2 (#4887) adds qk_vnni_128x4, an AMX kernel that scores one query group against one dense page by reading the VNNI-packed K plane of PR 1 as its B operand, and it removes PR 1's temporary gate that kept such pages off the dense AMX page path.

The page introduces one data model (the padded query rows and the typed K view the kernel takes) and one algorithm (the kernel's four-step tile loop), placed on the plane diagram K_VNNI-B1, the type model K_VNNI-B2 and the function model KV_CACHE-B3.
The shared block save of PR 3 and the page bits and the row-major tail block of PR 4 are not in this PR, so the diagrams that draw them are marked context or not involved.

words.definition: The first and the second matrix of one AMX tile multiply. The multiply accepts a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand. For qk_vnni_128x4 the padded query rows are A and the 16 K panels of the page are B; for qk_rowmajor_128x4 the native K page is A and the VNNI-packed queries are B.
Tile registers 0 to 3 of the AMX kernels. The tile multiply adds its products into them, so they hold the running sums. In qk_vnni_128x4 accumulator tile b holds the scores of token block b.
Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS consumes the VNNI layout as its B operand, and one 1 KiB panel is exactly one B tile.
The CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels and the code that selects them. Without it the AMX tests are placeholder cases and every page takes the software path.

The function of self_attention.hpp that applies one dense page to one query with the AMX QK kernel and the AMX PV kernel in one call. In this PR it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with page::k_packed under the layout gate and qk_rowmajor_128x4 with page::k otherwise [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1749, 1781-1787].

The per-page scoring function of self_attention.hpp. For one (query, page) pair it takes the dense AMX page path when the compile-time and run-time conditions hold, and otherwise scores the page with the reader qk_group (VNNI slot) or the dotter (row-major slot) [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1856, 1904-1910, 1994-1997].

The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer, one channel reader and writer per worker. They read a page only after every minibatch that writes it counted the latch down, and they only read K. The kernel of this PR runs on them.
Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. One register has 16 lanes of 32 bits. The reader qk_group is AVX-512 code with one token per lane.

bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values and of the queries the packers copy. fp32 (32-bit float) is the accumulation format of the score kernels. One bf16 step at 26.625 is 0.125.

16 consecutive tokens of a page, page offsets 16 c to 16 c + 15, c = 0 to 3 (k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16, TOKEN_BLOCKS_4). Its bytes are its 4 panels, one per dimension step, 4 KiB in all. In this PR every block of a VNNI slot holds the VNNI form.

PR 4's per-slot record of which 16-token blocks of a page hold the VNNI form: one bit per block in the atomic byte k_vnni_blocks_, read by page::k_vnni_blocks with acquire order. It does not exist at this PR.
PR 4's in-place conversions of one 16-token block between the row-major form and the VNNI form (h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp at PR 4). Not in this PR.

The unit of KV memory allocation of tron: it reserves space for a number of pages, owns that memory and hands out pages. Its public methods and the page's are the interface of kv_cache.hpp [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:832].

clear_kv_complete_at is the main-branch page function that resets a page offset when a new token takes it [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2185]. k_forget_row is PR 4's addition that drops the K bits of that offset and above. Both run between forward passes under the tree lock.

PR 4's forward-end conversion: save_k queues each block that a short run completed in pending_k_blocks_, and convert_pending_k_blocks converts the queued blocks after wait_for_coop_gof. Not in this PR.

copy_from copies a token range of every slot from another page (main branch, kv_cache.hpp:2322). copy_storage_slot does it for one storage slot; PR 1 made a whole-page copy one owner assignment and a smaller range a token-by-token copy_token (load_row then store_row) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2280, 2289; h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:334-341]. PR 4 adds the bits to the copy.
Prefill is the phase that scores the prompt tokens of a request; its wall time is the TTFT. Decode is the generation phase where every step saves one token per user; its rate is the TPS.

words.term: dense page / dense AMX page path
words.definition: A dense page is a full 64-token page that the query sees whole and inside its sliding window (is_dense_amx_page). The dense AMX page path applies such a page with the AMX QK and PV kernels. Its compile-time condition is amx_attn_h128g4::eligible and its run-time conditions are a packed query (amx_q_packed != nullptr) and is_dense_amx_page [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1904-1910].

A dimension step is 32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (k_vnni::STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16), the depth of one AMX tile multiply; a 128-dimension head has 4 steps. A pair is two adjacent dimensions of one token stored in one 32-bit dword.

The test that checks routing with stand-in kernels that count their calls instead of running AMX. In this PR the fakes of both packers and both QK kernels count into one probe, and the VNNI packer counts a second time, so the test checks that the packer of the build's layout ran [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63, 171, 196, 260-272].

The per-token dot-product loop of self_attention.hpp (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp). It scores row-major K one token per call. In this PR it is compiled only for row-major slots; PR 4 lets it score the rows of a row-major tail block.
The extra physical slot of a book for the EAGLE speculation model. PR 4 gives it its own entry in the page's K-state arrays. Main-branch code otherwise.

amx_attn_h128g4::eligible is the compile-time gate of the AMX path: head size 128, kv_mul 4 and a bf16 query type [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:170-171]. is_dense_amx_page is the run-time check that a page is dense for one query [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1725].

book::fill_random is the test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values; fill_storage_slot is its body for one storage slot. PR 1 made it reach a VNNI plane through k_vnni_access::plane, the one documented exception to the typed access rule [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1290, 1715, 1721].

A run that feeds every binary a fixed token sequence through --force-feed-text-token-file, so all binaries score the same context at every step. The PR body uses one to show that the token-247 difference is an exact tie.

The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after run() joined the workers and wait_for_coop_gof returned [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1834, 1838]. PR 4 converts the queued blocks there. Nothing runs there in this PR.

The FPGA (field-programmable gate array) is the card that scores attention in hardware. cached_operation_uses_hw says once per model whether an operation's K is scored there [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1529]. PR 4 keeps the blocks of such operations row-major; this PR has no hardware-attention policy.

words.term: GOF staging gather (gof::populate, k_head_fn, help_drain_gof, wait_for_coop_gof)
words.definition: A GOF is a group of four tokens of K/V data that gof::populate copies into a buffer for the FPGA [src/tron/gof.cpp:188]. page_info::k_head_fn returns one token's K row; PR 1 made it gather the row from a VNNI plane with page::get_k_row [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2759]. Idle attention workers run the staging through help_drain_gof and the main thread drains the rest in wait_for_coop_gof [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3239, 3252].

The case "AMX QK from the VNNI K plane is bit-identical to AMX QK from row-major K" of t_amx_numerics. It stores the same K row-major and, through store_row in scrambled token order, VNNI-packed, packs the same queries both ways, runs both kernels on real AMX and compares the 4 x 64 fp32 scores bit for bit for 2 seeds. Without AMX hardware it returns early with a warning [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:219-279].

PR 3's protocol in which the main thread cuts a minibatch into work units (k_store_cut_units), opens a window (opened), every thread of the window claims units (next_unit) and stores them with store_k_block, the helpers leave (finished) and main joins under a watchdog (k_join_clock_spins). k_store_shared decides whether a store is shared; worker_ix and n_workers name the threads. Not in this PR.
PR 4's third condition of the dense AMX page path: page::k_vnni_blocks must say that all 4 blocks of the page are VNNI. In this PR the path has two run-time conditions only.

The read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane for a slot and KV head, VNNI slots only [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1997-2001]. In this PR it is the argument of both score kernels: qk_vnni_128x4 reads it in place as its B operand and qk_group reads it one token per lane.
PR 4's per-slot record of the saved K rows of a page (one bit per page offset) and the two functions that set the bits after a row store and after a whole-block store. Not in this PR.

The index map of the VNNI plane: index(token, dim) gives the element position of one value from its token block, dimension step, pair, token column and half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:107-114]. The worked example maps token 37, dimension 70 to element 5226.

detail::k_vnni_access::plane(view), the one route from a packed K view to its raw plane address [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:212-219]. It is open to the typed operations of the header, the two score kernels (qk_group and, from this PR, qk_vnni_128x4) and the test-only fill.

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128> owns one 16 KiB VNNI-packed K plane as a 64-byte-aligned bf16 array [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:183-204]. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128> (T = bf16 or const bf16, the concept k_vnni_element) is the only way to name a plane; a writable view converts to a read-only one, never back [127, 137-172]. Views come only from an owner's as_view().

amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4, added here: the AMX kernel that computes S = Q x K^T for one dense page whose K is VNNI-packed, with the padded query rows as the A operand and the 16 K panels as the B operand, writing s[4][64] fp32 unscaled scores [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:237-303; h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:252-268].

TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment prevents use of the AMX kernels at run time. A VNNI-packed binary then scores every page with the reader qk_group: an AMX-off run of the same layout, not a rollback to the row-major numerics.

A KV head is one key/value head of grouped-query attention. kv_mul is the number of query heads per KV head: 4 for qwen3-4b and llama-3.1-8b. A query group is the kv_mul query heads that share one KV head; the AMX kernels take groups of 4.

The struct holding the two planes K and V of one (storage slot, KV head, page) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2519]. KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 names the plane count. PR 1 made its member k the typed owner k_vnni_tensor for a VNNI slot (k_storage) [2526-2536].

kv_saves_ is the page's per-offset, per-slot count of saved K and V (main branch, kv_cache.hpp:2213). After each row store save_k_impl marks the token with mark_k_complete, credits the GOF under hardware attention (credit_gof_save) and counts the latch down [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3126, 3130, 3135]. The trace label 'WK roped' is logged before them [3094].

batch::upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot countdown object that the downstream attention waits on [h/tron/models/common.hpp:1160]. save_k counts it down once per downstream minibatch after all its row stores [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3135].

k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, a compile-time constant that is true only for 128-dimension heads and only when the option is on [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:99-102]. In this PR it picks the packer and the kernel at the two AMX sites of self_attention.hpp.
The main branch of the tron repository, the base of PR 1. Code marked 'main' on this page exists there unchanged by the stack.

words.term: main thread / main helpers / run() / run_main_help / TronCpp.hs
words.definition: The main thread runs the generated plugin's run(), which calls save_k; the main helpers are its helper threads, which run the generated run_main_help [ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:1364, 1420, 2918-2921]. TronCpp.hs is the Haskell generator of the plugins. PR 3 makes run_main_help call save_k with the helper's worker_ix.

words.term: minibatch / batch / items / token_jobs_do_kv / K buffer ks
words.definition: A minibatch (struct batch) is one chunk of a forward pass's token jobs, its items [h/tron/models/common.hpp:991, 1083]. token_jobs_do_kv says per job whether it needs KV work [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1158]. ks is the K buffer of one layer that save_k reads [3079].
A deliberate code change that a test must catch. For this PR: with the kernel's second panel load changed from token block 1 to block 2, the identity case fails at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:275.

words.term: native K view (page::k, kv_block::k_view, k_at, const_native_k_view)
words.definition: The row-major views of a K plane: page::k returns the kv_block's k_view, a [token][element] view, and k_at(i_page) one token's row [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1923-1984, 2554-2572]. PR 1 constrained all of them to row-major slots. const_native_k_view is the argument type of qk_rowmajor_128x4.

The comment block in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (line 17) that states the gates of the AMX path and its numerics contract: the AMX path differs from the AVX-512 path in the bf16 rounding of the PV weights and in the fp32 add order.

The comment block in h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp (line 651) that says who writes and who reads the VNNI K layout. This PR rewrites its Why paragraph, its consumer items 2 and 3 and its kill-switch paragraph for the kernel [663-674, 683-694, 709-713].

The comment block in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (lines 195-229) that explains the flipped operand roles: the row-major kernel computes S^T = K x Q^T and transposes in registers; with VNNI-packed K the kernel computes S = Q x K^T with no transpose. This PR adds its VNNI paragraph [222-229].

PR 3's comment block in model.hpp that records why save_k was the main thread's largest serial piece of a prefill layer with the per-row store (0.86 ms per layer, measured 2026-09-14) and the two remedies: the block save and the sharing with the main helpers. Not in this PR.

The comment block in h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp (line 94) that says a tile store writes 16 rows, so both QK kernels store into an internal buffer and copy only the 4 query rows out. s16 is that buffer in qk_vnni_128x4, 16 rows x 64 fp32 [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:247, 296-302].
The CMake option, off by default, that selects VNNI-packed K for every 128-dimension head. It stays off in every build preset until PR 4.

words.term: packers (pack_q_group_128x4, pack_q_rows_128x4) / query pack / query-pack slot (amx_qpack_slot)
words.definition: The packers prepare the queries of one group: pack_q_group_128x4 (main branch) packs the 4 rows into the VNNI layout as the B operand of the row-major kernel; pack_q_rows_128x4 (this PR) copies the 4 rows as stored into rows 0 to 3 of a 16-row A operand [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:136, 225-229]. A query pack is one packer call for one query token, into a query-pack slot, one 4,096-byte buffer per query token that serves either packer [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:256-263, 1690-1713].

A block of 64 contiguous tokens of KV data (page_size), the unit by which attention proceeds [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1825-1827]. A page struct is a lightweight reference into a book and keeps the per-token save counters.

words.term: page K-state helpers of PR 4 (k_state_ix, k_storage_ref, k_storage_of, eagle_view_active, k_block_bits, k_block_is_vnni, block_bit, offset_bit, k_with_storage_geometry, k_storage_readable)
words.definition: The helpers PR 4 adds around the two bit arrays: which state entry and which storage slot a call means, the bit masks of one block or one offset, the acquire read of a block bit, and whether a storage slot can be read. None exists at this PR.

One 64-byte line of a panel: one dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens, 32 bf16 = 16 dwords. The 16 pair rows of a panel are 64 bytes apart, and one pair row is one 64-byte tile row of the kernel's B tile.

The 1 KiB part of a K plane for one 32-dimension step s and one 16-token block c: 16 pair rows of 64 bytes, at index s * 4 + c [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:76-79]. A plane holds 16 panels. A panel is exactly one AMX B tile, which the kernel's static_asserts pin [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:257-268].

words.term: per-row store (store_row, load_row, set_k_row, get_k_row, pair_base, pair_row_offsets)
words.definition: PR 1's way of writing one token's 128-dimension row into the VNNI plane: store_row issues 4 scatters of 16 dwords, one per dimension step, into the token's column of its block's 4 panels, and load_row is the inverse gather [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:294-306, 313-325]. page::set_k_row and page::get_k_row call them for a VNNI slot and memcpy for a row-major slot [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2040]. pair_base and pair_row_offsets are their address helpers [264-283]. In this PR save_k stores every row this way [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3113, 3118].
K for one KV head of one page: 64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB, the same bytes as the row-major plane. For a VNNI slot kv_block::k owns it as a k_vnni_tensor.
A pull request of the tron repository. PR 1 is #4868, PR 2 (this page) is #4887, PR 3 is #4898, PR 4 is #4901; each is based on the previous one and all four replace PR #4424.
The prompt length in tokens of a measurement cell (the runtron flag --prompt-length). Every run then generates 256 tokens.

k_vnni::qk_group, PR 1's AVX-512 routine that scores a query group against one VNNI-packed page, one token per vector lane, for the tokens set in a live mask [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp:60-62]. In this PR it serves every page the kernel does not take: partial or partly visible pages, the kill switch, hosts without AMX, builds without AMX dispatch, and the shapes and query types outside the AMX gate.

The AMX QK kernel of main for a row-major K page: K is the A operand and Q is VNNI-packed as the B operand; the result is transposed in AVX-512 registers on the way out [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:156; h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:237].
The 4-billion-parameter model of the PR body's measurements, with kv_mul 4 and 128-dimension heads.
The CI documentation of tron. This PR adds the paragraph that says the identity case compiles in every AMX-dispatch build and executes AMX only on a Granite Rapids runner [README.ci.md:597-600].
One row of head_size bf16 values per token, the K layout of main and of every head size other than 128 under the option. A row-major slot keeps the native K views and the dotter.

words.term: row-major tail block (row_major_row, store_row_major, load_row_major, k_row_if_row_major)
words.definition: PR 4's form of an incomplete 16-token block of a VNNI slot: token t owns 256 contiguous bytes until all 16 rows are saved, then the block is converted in place. row_major_row addresses such a row, store_row_major and load_row_major copy it, and page::k_row_if_row_major hands it to the FPGA staging. None exists at this PR.

save_k (two overloads) stores the K rows of one minibatch for one layer and calls save_k_impl [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3077, 3139, 3147]. At this PR save_k_impl stores every row on the main thread inside its per-token loop, with set_k_row for a VNNI slot and page::k(...).set for a row-major slot [3092-3135]. save_v is the V counterpart [3155].

Q is the query matrix, K the key matrix and S = Q x K^T the score matrix of one query group against the tokens of one page. The AMX kernels write the raw, unscaled scores into s_pages[head][token], 4 rows of 64 fp32, the array the software loop also fills [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1776-1787].

PR 3's whole-block store: store_block transposes the 16 rows of a block in registers (transpose_16x16_epi32) and writes them as 64 whole lines; page::set_k_block calls it for one KV head; store_k_block in model.hpp stores one work unit of a minibatch. None exists at this PR.
The span of past tokens the model attends to. A page outside it is not dense for the query.

A slot is one persistent K/V storage region of a book, selected by kv_slot_id [h/tron/attention_ids.hpp:23]. A storage slot (kv_storage_offset) is the absolute offset of such a region in the book's physical allocation [h/tron/models/common.hpp:240]. A VNNI-packed slot is one whose K uses the VNNI layout.
The generated run() waits for the K channel, the roped K rows of every token of the minibatch, before it calls save_k. startOperand is the generator's name for that wait (ingest/src/TronCpp.hs).

The AMX tile instruction (_tile_dpbf16ps) that multiplies a bf16 A tile by a bf16 B tile and adds the fp32 products into an accumulator tile. Each score element is the same dot product of 16 dimension pairs whichever operand holds K, which is why both kernels agree bit for bit.

The clause && !k_vnni::layout_on<operation_head_size> that PR 1 placed on the dense AMX page path, sending every page of a VNNI-packed slot to the reader. This PR removes it [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1904-1905].
An AMX register of 16 rows by 64 bytes. The kernels of amx_attn.cpp use 8 tiles: accumulators 0 to 3 and operand tiles 4 to 6 [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:40-63].

TPS is tokens per second, the decode throughput. TTFT is the time to first token, the prefill wall time. The PR body's decision band is twice the larger sample standard deviation over 3 repetitions, never smaller than 0.4 TPS or 0.15 s.

PR 1's typed view of one token's 128 bf16 values in dimension order with the caller's alignment and DMA (direct memory access) flags, not packed storage [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:222-231]. k_source_row builds a read-only row and k_destination_row a writable one [237-256]. The identity case builds its rows with k_source_row [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:252].
The lock on the scheduler's token tree. Page clears and copies run between forward passes while it is held, so no forward pass reads the book then.
The inference program under test. runtron is its command-line tool.

A compile-time check in t_llama_unit (a requires expression under STATIC_REQUIRE) that the kernel accepts k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> and its writable form, and rejects const bf16*, bf16*, the native K view and the V view [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:103-106, 428-434].
The owner and the typed view of the packed V plane of a kv_block, unchanged by the stack [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2541, 2546]. The kernel rejects it as its K argument.

VNNI: Vector Neural Network Instructions. In the VNNI layout two consecutive dimensions of one token are adjacent in memory, and one 64-byte line holds that dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens. It is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply. VNNI-packed means stored in this layout.
The example the three source pages trace: token 37, dimension 70 of the K plane of storage slot 5, KV head 0, page 7, at element 5226 of the VNNI form (panel #10, pair row 3, dword 5).

what_lands.concept: Note [QK orientation]: the flipped operand roles
what_lands.where: h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:195-229 (the VNNI paragraph at 222-229); the dispatch note lines 27-29; the flow chart line 63
what_lands.note: The AMX tile multiply takes a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand. With VNNI-packed K the kernel computes S = Q x K^T with Q as A and the 16 K panels as B, so the register transpose of the row-major kernel is not needed.

what_lands.concept: The padded query rows: pack_q_rows_128x4 and the shared query-pack slot
what_lands.note: The packer copies the 4 query rows of a group (1 KiB) into rows 0 to 3 of a 16-row A operand whose rows 4 to 15 stay zero. The 4 KiB query-pack slot is the size of the row-major packer's output, so one slot serves either packer.

what_lands.concept: qk_vnni_128x4: the AMX QK kernel on the VNNI plane
what_lands.where: src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:58-63 (the tile names), 231-303 (the kernel); declaration h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:252-268
what_lands.note: The padded Q rows load into tile 4; in each of the 4 dimension steps the panels of token blocks 0 to 3 load into tiles 5 and 6 and multiply into accumulator tiles 0 to 3. The four 16-row tile stores go to the internal buffer s16 and only the 4 query rows are copied out, so the scores land as S[query][token] with no transpose.

what_lands.concept: The typed boundary: the kernel takes k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> and is the second user of k_vnni_access::plane
what_lands.note: The kernel's K argument is the read-only view that page::k_packed returns, and it reaches the raw plane address only through detail::k_vnni_access::plane. Six compile-time checks pin that the kernel accepts the view and rejects raw pointers, the native K view and the V view.

what_lands.concept: Dispatch by the layout gate: packer and kernel per build, the temporary gate removed
what_lands.note: At the pack site k_vnni::layout_on picks pack_q_rows_128x4 for a VNNI-packed slot, and at the dense-page site it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with page::k_packed. The clause && !k_vnni::layout_on that PR 1 placed on the dense AMX page path is removed, and every other page keeps the reader qk_group.

what_lands.concept: The identity case, its mutation check, the dispatch-test fakes, the typed-boundary probe and the CI note
what_lands.note: The identity case stores the same K row-major and VNNI-packed, packs the same queries both ways, runs both kernels on real AMX and compares the 4 x 64 fp32 scores bit for bit for 2 seeds. The dispatch test's fakes of both packers and both kernels count into one probe and check that the packer of the build's layout ran.

walkthrough.say: Start at the plane: one K plane is 16 panels of 1 KiB, one per (dimension step s, token block c), and a panel is 16 pair rows of 64 bytes. Point at the panel (s, c) box and the pair row box: a panel is exactly one AMX B tile, and that is the whole reason for the layout. Open src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:257-268, where five static_asserts pin the drawing to the tile, and 279-294, where each tile load takes panel (step * 4 + block). Nothing of this diagram changes in this PR.

Open Note [QK orientation] at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:195-229. The AMX tile multiply takes a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand, so main's kernel computes S^T = K x Q^T with K as A and VNNI-packed Q as B, and transposes the result in registers. With VNNI-packed K the roles flip: Q is A, the panels are B, S = Q x K^T comes out in the orientation the softmax step wants, and no transpose is needed (lines 222-229).

Now the kernel, src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:237-303. The padded Q rows load into tile 4 (line 278); in each of the 4 dimension steps the panels of token blocks 0 to 3 load into tiles 5 and 6 and each multiplies into accumulator tile 0 to 3 (279-294). The four 16-row tile stores go to the buffer s16 (296-299) and only rows 0 to 3 are copied out (300-302). The packer pack_q_rows_128x4 at 225-229 is a 1 KiB memcpy into rows 0 to 3 of a zeroed 4 KiB query-pack slot.

Point at the new box amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4 and the route from k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> through detail::k_vnni_access::plane. The kernel's K argument is the type page::k_packed returns (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1997), and the one raw-address call is amx_attn.cpp:244. The typed-boundary probe in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:428-434 checks that the kernel accepts the view and rejects raw pointers, the native K view and the V view. The owner, the views and the reader qk_group in this diagram are PR 1.

Point at the apply_page_tok / apply_dense_amx_page caller row and the new qk_vnni_128x4 cell. Open h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1707-1711, where the layout gate picks pack_q_rows_128x4 or pack_q_group_128x4, and 1781-1787, where it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with k_packed or qk_rowmajor_128x4 with page::k. Then 1904-1910: the temporary gate clause of PR 1 is gone, so a dense page of a VNNI slot takes the AMX path. Every other page keeps the reader qk_group (1994-1997), as Note [K VNNI storage] items 2 and 3 now say (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:683-694).

On the lanes, the kernel sits in the attention-worker box next to qk_group: it runs on an attention worker, reads the plane through the same route and writes only its own score buffer (amx_attn.cpp:244, 247). No thread rule changes in this PR. The save_k lanes of PR 3 and the forward-end conversion of PR 4 are not here yet.

Use this diagram to say what is not yet true. At this PR a VNNI slot has one form only, because every row enters through store_row (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2010-2022), so the kernel reads all 16 panels with no per-block check (amx_attn.cpp:277-295). The row-major form, the block bit and the k_layout_dense gate are PR 4.

pr.title: Use VNNI K layout in AMX attention
pr.head: 0ee8671d35

short_version: PR 2 (#4887) adds qk_vnni_128x4, an AMX kernel that scores one query group against one dense page by reading the VNNI-packed K plane of PR 1 as its B operand, and it removes PR 1's temporary gate that kept such pages off the dense AMX page path.

The page places one data model (the typed K view the kernel takes) and one algorithm (the kernel's four-step tile loop) on the plane diagram K_VNNI-B1, the type model K_VNNI-B2 and the function model KV_CACHE-B3, and the padded query rows have no base diagram.
The shared block save of PR 3, the two bit arrays of the page and the row-major tail block of PR 4 are not in this PR, and the diagrams that draw them are marked context or not involved.

words.definition: The first and the second matrix of one AMX tile multiply. The multiply accepts a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand. For qk_vnni_128x4 the padded query rows are A and the 16 K panels of the page are B. For qk_rowmajor_128x4 the native K page is A and the VNNI-packed queries are B.
Tile registers 0 to 3 of the AMX kernels. The tile multiply adds its products into them, so they hold the running sums. In qk_vnni_128x4 accumulator tile b holds the scores of token block b.
Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set of the CPU. Its tile multiply TDPBF16PS consumes the VNNI layout as its B operand, and one 1 KiB panel is exactly one B tile.
The CMake option that compiles the AMX kernels and the code that selects them. Without it the AMX tests are placeholder cases and every page takes the software path.

The function of self_attention.hpp that applies one dense page to one query with the AMX QK kernel and the AMX PV kernel in one call. In this PR it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with page::k_packed under the layout gate and qk_rowmajor_128x4 with page::k otherwise [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1749, 1781-1787].

The per-page scoring function of self_attention.hpp. For one (query, page) pair it takes the dense AMX page path when the compile-time and run-time conditions hold, and otherwise scores the page with the reader qk_group (VNNI slot) or the dotter (row-major slot) [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1856, 1904-1910, 1994-1997].

The threads that run the attention kernels of a layer, one channel reader and writer per worker. They read a page only after every minibatch that writes it counted the latch down, and they never write K. The kernel of this PR runs on them.
Advanced Vector Extensions, the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. One register has 16 lanes of 32 bits. The reader qk_group is AVX-512 code with one token per lane.

bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format of the stored K and V values and of the queries the packers copy. fp32 (32-bit float) is the accumulation format of the score kernels. One bf16 step at 26.625 is 0.125.

16 consecutive tokens of a page, page offsets 16 c to 16 c + 15, c = 0 to 3 (k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16, TOKEN_BLOCKS_4). Its bytes are its 4 panels, one per dimension step, 4 KiB in all. In this PR every block of a VNNI slot holds the VNNI form.

PR 4's per-slot record of which 16-token blocks of a page hold the VNNI form: one bit per block in the atomic byte k_vnni_blocks_, read by page::k_vnni_blocks with acquire order. It does not exist at this PR.
PR 4's in-place conversions of one 16-token block between the row-major form and the VNNI form (h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp at PR 4). Not in this PR.

The unit of KV memory allocation of tron: it reserves space for a number of pages, owns that memory and hands out pages. Its public methods and the page's are the interface of kv_cache.hpp [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:832].

clear_kv_complete_at is the main-branch page function that resets a page offset when a new token takes it [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2185]. k_forget_row is PR 4's addition that drops the K bits of that offset and above. Both run between forward passes under the tree lock.

PR 4's forward-end conversion: save_k queues each block that a short run completed in pending_k_blocks_, and convert_pending_k_blocks converts the queued blocks after wait_for_coop_gof. Not in this PR.

copy_from copies a token range of every slot from another page (main branch, kv_cache.hpp:2322). copy_storage_slot does it for one storage slot. PR 1 made a whole-page copy one owner assignment and a smaller range a token-by-token copy_token (load_row then store_row) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2280, 2296, 2298-2301; h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:334-341]. PR 4 adds the bits to the copy.
Prefill is the phase that scores the prompt tokens of a request. Its wall time is the TTFT. Decode is the generation phase where every step saves one token per user. Its rate is the TPS.

words.term: dense page / dense AMX page path
words.definition: A dense page is a full 64-token page that the query sees whole and inside its sliding window (is_dense_amx_page). The dense AMX page path applies such a page with the AMX QK and PV kernels. Its compile-time condition is amx_attn_h128g4::eligible and its run-time conditions are a packed query (amx_q_packed != nullptr) and is_dense_amx_page [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1904-1910].

A dimension step is 32 dimensions = 16 dimension pairs (k_vnni::STEP_DIMS_32, STEP_PAIRS_16), the depth of one AMX tile multiply. A 128-dimension head has 4 steps. A pair is two adjacent dimensions of one token stored in one 32-bit dword.

The test that checks routing with stand-in kernels that count their calls instead of running AMX. In this PR the fakes of both packers and both QK kernels count into one probe, and the VNNI packer counts a second time. The test therefore checks that the packer of the build's layout ran [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63, 171, 196, 260-274].

The per-token dot-product loop of self_attention.hpp (struct dotter in h/tron/kernels/dotter.hpp). It scores row-major K one token per call. In this PR it is compiled only for row-major slots. PR 4 lets it score the rows of a row-major tail block.
The extra physical slot of a book for the EAGLE speculation model. PR 4 gives it its own entry in the page's K-state arrays. Main-branch code otherwise.

amx_attn_h128g4::eligible is the compile-time gate of the AMX path: head size 128, kv_mul 4 and a bf16 query type [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:170-171]. is_dense_amx_page is the run-time check that a page is dense for one query [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1725].

book::fill_random is the test-only fill of every kv_block with random bf16 values. fill_storage_slot is its body for one storage slot. PR 1 made it reach a VNNI plane through k_vnni_access::plane, the one documented exception to the typed access rule [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1290, 1715, 1721].

A run that feeds every binary a fixed token sequence through --force-feed-text-token-file, so all binaries score the same context at every step. The PR body uses one to show that the token-247 difference is an exact tie.

The end of one forward pass on the main thread, after run() joined the workers and wait_for_coop_gof returned [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1834, 1838]. PR 4 converts the queued blocks there. Nothing runs there in this PR.

The FPGA (field-programmable gate array) is the card that scores attention in hardware. cached_operation_uses_hw says once per model whether an operation's K is scored there [h/tron/models/model.hpp:1529]. PR 4 keeps the blocks of such operations row-major. This PR has no hardware-attention policy.

words.term: GOF staging gather (gof::populate, k_head_fn, help_drain_gof, wait_for_coop_gof)
words.definition: A GOF is a group of four tokens of K/V data that gof::populate copies into a buffer for the FPGA [src/tron/gof.cpp:188]. page_info::k_head_fn returns one token's K row. PR 1 made it gather the row from a VNNI plane with page::get_k_row [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2747-2759]. Idle attention workers run the staging through help_drain_gof and the main thread drains the rest in wait_for_coop_gof [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3239, 3252].

The case "AMX QK from the VNNI K plane is bit-identical to AMX QK from row-major K" of t_amx_numerics. It stores the same K row-major and, through store_row in scrambled token order, VNNI-packed, packs the same queries both ways, runs both kernels on real AMX and compares the 4 x 64 fp32 scores bit for bit for 2 seeds. Without AMX hardware it returns early with a warning [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:219-279].

PR 3's protocol in which the main thread cuts a minibatch into work units (k_store_cut_units), opens a window (opened), every thread of the window claims units (next_unit) and stores them with store_k_block, the helpers leave (finished) and main joins under a watchdog (k_join_clock_spins). k_store_shared decides whether a store is shared. worker_ix and n_workers name the threads. Not in this PR.
PR 4's third condition of the dense AMX page path: page::k_vnni_blocks must say that all 4 blocks of the page are VNNI. In this PR the path has two run-time conditions only.

The read-only typed view (k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128>) of one page's K plane for a slot and KV head, VNNI slots only [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1997-2001]. In this PR it is the argument of both score kernels: qk_vnni_128x4 reads it in place as its B operand and qk_group reads it one token per lane.
PR 4's per-slot record of the saved K rows of a page (one bit per page offset) and the two functions that set the bits after a row store and after a whole-block store. Not in this PR.

The index map of the VNNI plane: index(token, dim) gives the element position of one value from its token block, dimension step, pair, token column and half [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:107-114]. The worked example maps token 37, dimension 70 to element 5226.

detail::k_vnni_access::plane(view), the one route from a packed K view to its raw plane address [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:212-219]. It is open to the typed operations of the header, the two score kernels (qk_group and, from this PR, qk_vnni_128x4) and the test-only fill.

k_vnni_tensor<64, 128> owns one 16 KiB VNNI-packed K plane as a 64-byte-aligned bf16 array [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:183-204]. k_vnni_view<T, 64, 128> (T = bf16 or const bf16, the concept k_vnni_element) is the only way to name a plane. A writable view converts to a read-only one, never back [127, 137-172]. Views come only from an owner's as_view().

amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4, added here: the AMX kernel that computes S = Q x K^T for one dense page whose K is VNNI-packed, with the padded query rows as the A operand and the 16 K panels as the B operand, writing s[4][64] fp32 unscaled scores [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:237-303; h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:252-268].

TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 in the environment prevents use of the AMX kernels at run time. A VNNI-packed binary then scores every page with the reader qk_group: an AMX-off run of the same layout, not a rollback to the row-major numerics.

A KV head is one key/value head of grouped-query attention. kv_mul is the number of query heads per KV head: 4 for qwen3-4b and llama-3.1-8b. A query group is the kv_mul query heads that share one KV head. The AMX kernels take groups of 4.

The struct holding the two planes K and V of one (storage slot, KV head, page) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2519]. KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 names the plane count. PR 1 made its member k the typed owner k_vnni_tensor for a VNNI slot (k_storage) [2526-2536].

kv_saves_ is the page's per-offset, per-slot count of saved K and V (main branch, kv_cache.hpp:2213). After all KV heads' rows of a token are stored, save_k_impl marks the token with mark_k_complete and, under hardware attention, credits the GOF (credit_gof_save) [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3126, 3130]. After the token loop it counts the latch down once per downstream minibatch [3134-3135]. The trace label 'WK roped' (the K rows after rope, the rotary position embedding, was applied) is logged before them [3094].

batch::upstream_kvs_ready is the per-slot countdown object that the downstream attention waits on [h/tron/models/common.hpp:1160]. save_k counts it down once per downstream minibatch after all its row stores [h/tron/models/model.hpp:3135].

k_vnni::layout_on<head_size>, a compile-time constant that is true only for 128-dimension heads and only when the option is on [h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp:99-102]. In this PR it picks the packer and the kernel at the two AMX sites of self_attention.hpp.
The main branch of the tron repository, the base of PR 1. Code marked 'main' on this page exists there unchanged by the stack.

walkthrough.say: Start at the plane: one K plane is 16 panels of 1 KiB, one per (dimension step s, token block c), and a panel is 16 pair rows of 64 bytes. Point at the panel (s, c) box and the pair row box: a panel is exactly one AMX B tile, and that is the whole reason for the layout. Open src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:257-268, where five static_asserts pin the drawing to the tile, and 279-294, where each tile load takes panel (step * 4 + block). No box of this diagram changes in this PR.

Open Note [QK orientation] at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:195-229: the AMX tile multiply takes a row-major matrix only as its A operand and needs the VNNI layout for its B operand. Main's kernel therefore computes S^T = K x Q^T with K as A and VNNI-packed Q as B, and transposes the result in registers. With VNNI-packed K the roles flip: Q is A and the panels are B. S = Q x K^T then comes out in the orientation the softmax step (the scaling and exponentiation of the scores in the caller) wants, with no transpose (lines 222-229).

Point at the box amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4, the kernel this PR adds, and the route from k_vnni_view<const bf16, 64, 128> through detail::k_vnni_access::plane. The kernel's K argument is the type page::k_packed returns (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:1997), and the one raw-address call is amx_attn.cpp:244. The typed-boundary probe in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:428-434 checks that the kernel accepts the view and rejects raw pointers, the native K view and the V view. The owner, the views and the reader qk_group in this diagram are PR 1.

First the A operand: pack_q_rows_128x4 at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:225-229 is a 1 KiB memcpy of the 4 query rows into rows 0 to 3 of a zeroed 4 KiB query-pack slot (h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:256-263), and rows 4 to 15 stay zero. Now the kernel, 237-303: the padded Q rows load into tile 4 (line 278). In each of the 4 dimension steps the panels of token blocks 0 to 3 load into tiles 5 and 6 and each multiplies into accumulator tile 0 to 3 (279-294). The four 16-row tile stores go to the buffer s16 (296-299) and only rows 0 to 3 are copied out (300-302).

Point at the apply_page_tok / apply_dense_amx_page caller row and the qk_vnni_128x4 cell. Open h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1707-1711 (the layout gate picks the packer) and 1781-1787 (it picks qk_vnni_128x4 with k_packed or qk_rowmajor_128x4 with page::k).
